questions.q: By how much does the Monte Carlo standard error shrink if you quadruple the number of simulated paths N?
options: It shrinks to a quarter of its original value
It shrinks by half, since standard error scales as σ_g/√N
It shrinks to zero immediately
It does not change at all
questions.explain: Standard error scales as σ_g/√N, so quadrupling N (4x) only reduces the standard error by a factor of √4 = 2, i.e. it is cut in half.

questions.q: Under the risk-neutral pricing formula, how is the fair price of a European call option computed?
options: C_0 = E[S_T] − K
C_0 = e^{-rT} · E^Q[max(S_T − K, 0)]
C_0 = S_0 − K, with no discounting
questions.explain: The fair price is the discounted risk-neutral expectation of the payoff: C_0 = e^{-rT}E^Q[max(S_T−K,0)], justified by the martingale pricing argument from the martingales lesson.

questions.q: In the Monte Carlo option-pricing code, why is S_T simulated using drift (r − ½σ²) rather than the stock's real-world expected return μ?
options: Because r and μ are interchangeable notations for the same quantity
Because pricing must use the risk-neutral measure, under which the drift is replaced by the risk-free rate r, as derived in the martingale and Itô's lemma lessons
Because using μ would make the code run faster
Because the risk-free rate is always zero
questions.explain: Risk-neutral pricing requires simulating under measure Q, where the GBM drift is r (not the real-world μ), which is exactly the setup that makes the discounted price process a martingale.

questions.q: What is the core idea behind the antithetic variates variance-reduction technique?
options: Running the entire simulation twice with the same random seed
Pairing each random draw Z with its mirror image −Z, averaging the resulting payoffs together, to reduce variance without extra independent sampling
Only simulating paths where the option ends up in the money
Increasing the strike price to simplify the payoff function
questions.explain: Antithetic variates pairs each draw Z with −Z and averages the corresponding payoffs, which tends to cancel sampling noise and reduce variance using the same underlying random numbers.

questions.q: How is the Monte Carlo option price validated in this lesson?
options: By checking that it is always exactly zero
By comparing it against the closed-form Black-Scholes price derived from d1 and d2
By comparing it to the strike price K
There is no way to validate a Monte Carlo price
questions.explain: The lesson computes the Black-Scholes closed-form price (using the standard d1, d2 formulas) and checks that the Monte Carlo estimate falls close to it and within its own confidence interval.
